item.title: about
item.description:
I’m Vidhi, a software engineer at Microsoft in Hyderabad. I work on the infrastructure that lets engineers test pre-production hardware (chips from NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel and AMD) before it ships. Before that I spent four years at VMware building the tools admins use to install, update and recover vCenter.

what pulls me in

I like the layer between hardware and the people using it. Most of my best work there has been about recovery: putting a device back to a known state, rolling back a failed update, or tracing a crash dump to a root cause. Good infrastructure is invisible, and I find that strangely satisfying.

item.title: cv
item.description:
experience

microsoft · software development engineer ii

hyderabad, india · jan 2025 – present

  • Lead architect of ALIS (Autonomous Lab Infra at Scale), a distributed platform that serves pre-production hardware to 100+ engineers. I grew it from an internal hackathon project into a system managing 150+ devices, scaling toward 300. I also re-architected it from a single instance into a distributed design.
  • Built clean device reallocation between users with automated reimaging and wipe-down. Added backup and recovery that restores a returning user’s device to their last saved state.
  • Redesigned ALIS authentication from a shared key to per-device onboarding via Azure Arc, closing a fleet-wide compromise risk.
  • Led bring-up of 4 new pre-production hardware platforms across NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel and AMD. Built the automation for remote reflashing and debugging so teams could use each platform early in its life.
  • Led power-state-transition and HLK validation on silicon that has since shipped, including NVIDIA RTX Spark and Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite / X2 Elite Extreme. This covered sleep-study analysis, driver compliance, crash-dump triage and root-cause analysis.
  • Validated ML model execution across successive ONNX Runtime execution-provider releases on CPU, GPU and NPU. The results informed which accelerator serves a given model on heterogeneous hardware.

vmware by broadcom · software development engineer ii

bangalore, india · aug 2020 – dec 2024

item.title: now
item.description:
A now page shows what I’m focused on these days.

at work

Scaling ALIS from 150 devices toward 300, and bringing up the next batch of pre-production hardware platforms.

learning

Systems for machine learning, starting from the ground up. I’m reading systems papers on:

  • GPU memory management and unified virtual memory (UVM)
  • kernel launch overhead, and how CUDA Graphs reduce it
  • tools that find memory bugs and races in GPU programs

I keep notes in plain English until each idea makes sense. Some of them will end up in notes/.

item.title: projects
item.description:
Hackathons and side projects, newest first. Work projects are internal, so there’s no code to link to, but I’m always happy to talk about them.

battery-aware power prioritization · 2026

Microsoft Garage Hackathon, 3rd place. You pick the one foreground app you care about. The tool gives it priority power and automatically hibernates idle background apps. The result was about 40% battery savings for the prioritized app.

alis ai-ops layer · 2025

An AI-Ops layer on top of ALIS, the lab platform I lead. It pairs a vector-search RAG pipeline for failure tracing with an LLM-based remediator. It cut mean time to repair by 40% across four mission-critical test suites: kstress, power state transition, HLK and BSP.
